source_text: Ubi tunc Marcion, Ponticus nauclerus, Stoicae studiosus? Ubi tunc Valentinus, Platonicae sectator? Nam constat illos neque adeo olim fuisse, Antonini fere principatu, et in catholicae primo doctrinam credidisse apud ecclesiam Romanensem sub episcopatu Eleutheri benedicti, donec ob inquietam semper curiositatem, qua fratres quoque vitiabant, semel et iterum eiecti, Marcion quidem cum ducentis sestertiis quae ecclesiae intulerat, novissime in perpetuum discidium relegati venena doctrinarum suarum disseminaverunt. Postmodum Marcion paenitentiam confessus cum condicioni datae sibi occurrit, ita pacem recepturus, si ceteros quos perditioni erudisset ecclesiae restitueret, morte praeventus est. Oportebat enim haereses esse. Nec tamen ideo bonum haereses quia esse eas oportebat. Quasi non et malum oportuerit esse. Nam et dominum tradi oportebat, sed vae traditori, ne quis etiam hinc haereses defendat. Si et Apellis stemma retractandum est, tam non vetus et ipse quam Marcion institutor et praeformator eius, sed lapsus in feminam desertor continentiae Marcionensis ab oculis sanctissimi magistri Alexandriam secessit. Inde post annos regressus non melior, nisi tantum qua iam non Marcionites, in alteram feminam impegit, illam virginem Philumenen, quam supra edidimus, postea vero immane prostibulum et ipsam, cuius energemate circumventus quae ab ea didicit Phaneroseis scripsit. Adhuc in saeculo supersunt qui meminerint eorum, etiam proprii discentes et successores ipsorum, ne posteriores negare possint. Quamquam et de operibus suis, ut dixit dominus, revincuntur. Si enim Marcion novum testamentum a vetere separavit, posterior est eo quod separavit, quia separare non posset nisi quod unitum fuit. Unitum ergo antequam separaretur postea factum separatum posteriorem ostendit separatorem. Item Valentinus aliter exponens et sine dubio emendans hoc nomine quicquid emendat, ut mendosum retro, alterius fuisse demonstrat. Hos ut insigniores et frequentiores adulteros veritatis nominamus. Ceterum et Nigidius nescio qui, et Hermogenes, et multi alii adhuc ambulant pervertentes vias domini. Ostendant mihi ex qua auctoritate prodierint? Si alium deum praedicant, quomodo eius dei rebus et litteris et nominibus utuntur adversus quem praedicant? si eundem, quomodo aliter? Probent se novos apostolos esse?, dicant Christum iterum descendisse, iterum ipsum docuisse, iterum crucifixum, iterum mortuum, iterum resuscitatum. Sic enim apostolus descripsit, sic enim apostolos solet facere, dare praeterea illis virtutem eadem signa edendi quae et ipse. Volo igitur et virtutes eorum proferri; nisi quod agnosco maximam virtutem eorum qua apostolos in perversum aemulantur. Illi enim de mortuis vivos faciebant, isti de vivis mortuos faciunt.
thought_title: Marcion and Valentinus as late innovators
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that heretics are later than the apostolic truth, and here he traces the careers of Marcion, Valentinus, and Apelles to show they are recent innovators.
pass_a_gloss: Where was Marcion then, the Pontic shipmaster, the student of Stoicism? Where was Valentinus then, the follower of the Platonic school? For it is agreed that they were not so very long ago, roughly in the principate of Antoninus, and that they first believed in the doctrine of the catholic church at the church of Rome under the episcopate of the blessed Eleutherus, until, because of their ever restless curiosity, by which they were also corrupting the brothers, they were expelled once and again, Marcion indeed with the two hundred sesterces which he had brought into the church, and at last they were banished into a perpetual separation and spread the poisons of their doctrines. Afterwards Marcion, having confessed repentance, when he met with the condition given to him, that he would receive peace if he restored to the church the rest whom he had trained for destruction, was prevented by death. For it was necessary that heresies exist. But heresies are not therefore good because it was necessary that they exist. As if it had not also been necessary that evil exist. For it was also necessary that the Lord be handed over, but woe to the betrayer, lest anyone also defend heresies from this. If also the pedigree of Apelles must be examined, he himself is not old, just as Marcion his founder and former, but having slipped into a woman, a deserter of Marcionite continence, he withdrew from the eyes of the most holy master to Alexandria. Thence having returned after years not better, except only in that he was no longer a Marcionite, he ran into another woman, that virgin Philumene, whom we mentioned above, but afterwards a huge prostitute also herself, and overcome by her spiritual activity he wrote the Phaneroseis which he learned from her. There are still in the world those who remember them, even their own disciples and successors, so that later generations cannot deny it. Although also by their own works, as the Lord said, they are convicted. For if Marcion separated the new testament from the old, he is later than that which he separated, because he could not separate except what had been united. Therefore what was united before it was afterwards made separated shows the separator to be later. Likewise Valentinus, expounding differently and without doubt emending, by this very name shows that whatever he emends, as previously faulty, belonged to another. These we name as the more notable and more frequent adulterers of the truth. Moreover also Nigidius, some one or other, and Hermogenes, and many others still walk about perverting the ways of the Lord. Let them show me from what authority they have come forth. If they preach another god, how do they use the things and writings and names of that god against whom they preach? If the same, how differently? Let them prove that they are new apostles: let them say that Christ has descended again, has himself taught again, has been crucified again, has died again, has been raised again. For thus the apostle described it, for thus he is accustomed to make apostles, to give them besides the power of producing the same signs which he himself also produced. I wish therefore that their powers also be brought forth; except that I recognize their greatest power by which they rival the apostles in a perverse way. For those made the living from the dead, these make the dead from the living.

choices.why: Keeps the genitive of the school with 'student' to show Marcion's philosophical training as Tertullian presents it.
Renders 'sectator' as 'follower' and keeps the adjective 'Platonicae' as 'of the Platonic school' to match the parallel with Marcion.

choices.english: first believed in the doctrine of the catholic church
choices.why: Keeps 'catholicae' as 'catholic church' and 'primo' as 'first' to show their initial orthodoxy before heresy.
rejected: at first believed the catholic doctrine
initially believed in the catholic teaching

choices.why: Literal rendering of 'venena' as 'poisons' preserves Tertullian's polemical metaphor.
Renders 'energemate' as 'spiritual activity' to convey the supernatural influence Tertullian attributes to Philumene.
Keeps the genitive 'of the truth' to preserve the metaphor of corrupting truth as adultery.

pass_b_english: Where then was Marcion, the shipmaster from Pontus, the student of Stoicism? Where then was Valentinus, the follower of the Platonic school? For it is agreed that they were not so very long ago—roughly in the reign of Antoninus—and that they first believed in the doctrine of the catholic church at Rome under the blessed bishop Eleutherus, until their restless curiosity, by which they were also corrupting the brothers, got them expelled once and then again. Marcion, indeed, was expelled with the two hundred sesterces he had brought into the church, and at last they were banished into permanent separation and scattered the poisons of their doctrines. Afterwards Marcion confessed repentance and accepted the condition offered him—that he would receive peace if he restored to the church the others he had trained for destruction—but he was overtaken by death. For heresies had to exist. Yet heresies are not good just because they had to exist. As if evil did not also have to exist. For the Lord also had to be betrayed, but woe to the betrayer—so let no one defend heresies even from this. If the pedigree of Apelles must also be examined, he is no more ancient than Marcion, his founder and shaper. But he became involved with a woman who had abandoned Marcion's discipline of continence, and withdrew from the eyes of his most holy teacher to Alexandria. Returning after some years, he was no better—except that he was no longer a Marcionite—and he crashed into another woman, that virgin Philumene whom we mentioned above, later herself a notorious prostitute. Overcome by her spiritual activity, he wrote the Phaneroseis based on what he learned from her. Even now there are people still alive in the world who remember them—their own disciples and successors—so that later generations cannot deny it. And indeed they are refuted by their own works, as the Lord said. For if Marcion separated the New Testament from the Old, he is later than what he separated, because he could not separate what had not been united. What was united before it was later separated shows that the separator came after. Likewise Valentinus, by expounding differently and no doubt correcting—by that very name, whatever he corrects he shows to have been faulty before and to have belonged to someone else. These are the ones we name as the more notable and frequent adulterers of the truth. But there is also some Nigidius or other, and Hermogenes, and many others still walking about perverting the ways of the Lord. Let them show me from what authority they have come forth. If they preach another god, how do they use the things, writings, and names of that God against whom they preach? If the same God, how do they do it differently? Let them prove they are new apostles: let them say Christ has come down again, taught again himself, been crucified again, died again, risen again. For that is how the apostle described it; that is how he is accustomed to make apostles—and to give them the power to produce the same signs he himself produced. I want their powers to be brought forward too—except that I recognize their greatest power, by which they rival the apostles in a perverse way. For the apostles made the living from the dead; these make the dead from the living.

problems.why: Latin says "ducentis sestertiis" (200 sesterces), not "two hundred thousand".
problems.ruling: Latin 'ducentis sestertiis' = 200 sesterces; English adds 'thousand,' changing the amount and misleading readers.

fixed: Changed 'two hundred thousand sesterces' to 'two hundred sesterces' because the source 'ducentis sestertiis' means 200 sesterces, not 200,000.

problems.quote: But he fell into a woman, a deserter of Marcion's continence
problems.why: 'Fell into a woman' is awkward; likely means he became involved with a woman who left Marcion's ascetic discipline.
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'he became involved with a woman who had abandoned Marcion's discipline of continence.'

problems.why: 'Huge prostitute' is odd English; likely means notorious or promiscuous, not physically large.
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'later a notorious prostitute' or 'a great harlot.'

edits.old: But he fell into a woman, a deserter of Marcion's continence, and withdrew
edits.new: But he became involved with a woman who had abandoned Marcion's discipline of continence, and withdrew

fixed: Source 'sed lapsus in feminam desertor continentiae Marcionensis' means he slipped into a woman, being a deserter of Marcionite continence; the English 'fell into a woman, a deserter of Marcion's continence' misreads the grammar. Rewrote to make the deserter Apelles, not the woman.
Source 'immane prostibulum' means a monstrous/notorious prostitute, not physically huge; changed 'huge' to 'notorious'.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'student of Stoic things/philosophy,' not 'of Stoicism' as a doctrine. Glossary maps philosophia to 'philosophy.'
last_rejected.ruling: Stoicae studiosus = student of Stoic philosophy; 'Stoicism' acceptable.
